Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-rays demonstrate bilateral upper lobe predominant fibrosis with pleural thickening and volume loss (indicated by arrows), which is the hallmark radiographic pattern of pleuroparenchymal fibroelastosis (PPFE). This condition is strongly associated with a history of pneumothorax and typically affects the apices, distinguishing it from the basilar-predominant patterns of asbestosis or advanced sarcoidosis.
